author: Staff Reporter
title: Beware of imitation sites posing as News24 - here's a reminder of what to look out for | News24
text:
News24 has become aware of a surge in scams targeting our readers across social media platforms, particularly Facebook.
Fraudsters are creating spoof websites that closely mimic the News24 brand, publishing fake articles, and in some cases, using deepfake technology to impersonate our journalists. These imitation sites are designed to steal personal information or promote fraudulent schemes which have no affiliation with News24.
“There is a concerted effort to exploit the credibility associated with our leading news brand to mislead the South African public. While we continue to invest in our own debunking and fact-checking resources to expose misinformation, we are not immune to these tactics of deception,” said News24 editor-in-chief Adriaan Basson.
“These online scammers are trading on the trust News24 has built with its readership, and we are asking our audience to be more vigilant,” he urged.

How the scams work:
Fake social media posts and websites engineered to look like News24 are being pushed through Facebook accounts, sponsored advertisements, and forwarded WhatsApp messages. Some may not immediately notice the discrepancies. However, the closer you look, the more the red flags reveal themselves.
If you are scrolling through social media or receiving forwarded content with untraceable origins, please be wary of these posts.
- Suspicious links: Only trust content from the website domain News24.com
- Clickbait or exaggerated headlines: Be wary of claims that feel too outrageous or urgent. Stop and verify.
- Content from unknown sources: If you cannot verify where a link originated, treat it with scepticism.
- Poor quality: Bad grammar and poorly written copy are often a red flag.
- Formatting: Distorted logos and layouts that do not match News24’s style.
- Requests for financial information: We will not ask you for your banking details via pop-up forms or social media.
- Platform verification: Check if posts are published via our Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp channels, which have the blue verified checkmark.
WARNING | Beware deepfake dupes impersonating News24 finance journalists ‘Maya and Bruce’
If you encounter a suspicious page or link claiming to be News24, please report it on the platform where possible. You can also reach out to our team at feedback@news24.com.
If you want to stay on the safe side, download the official News24 mobile app from either the Google Play Store, the App Store or the Huawei App Gallery, and follow News24 directly for trusted news.
